name: DIFC Data Protection Law (DIFC Law No. 5 of 2020)
description: Personal data processing under the DIFC Data Protection Law, DIFC Law No. 5 of 2020, as amended (Consolidated Version, July 2025): what a data processing agreement and the processing it governs must meet in the DIFC. English is the language of DIFC legislation. DRAFT: not yet legally reviewed.

clauses.source_title: Data Protection Law, DIFC Law No. 5 of 2020 (Consolidated Version, July 2025)

clauses.title: Lawfulness of Processing
clauses.source_title: Data Protection Law, DIFC Law No. 5 of 2020 (Consolidated Version, July 2025)

clauses.title: Processing of Special Categories of Personal Data
clauses.source_title: Data Protection Law, DIFC Law No. 5 of 2020 (Consolidated Version, July 2025)

clauses.title: Accountability and notification: technical and organisational measures
clauses.content:
A Controller or Processor is required to implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to demonstrate that Processing is performed in accordance with this Law, including:
(a) taking into account:
(i) the nature, scope, context and purpose of the Processing;
(ii) the risks presented by the Processing to a relevant Data Subject; and
(iii) prevailing information security good industry practice.
(b) ensuring a level of security:
(i) appropriate to the risks associated with Processing, taking account of any wilful, negligent, accidental, unauthorised or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, disclosure of or access to Personal Data; and
(ii) against all other unlawful forms of Processing;
(c) ensuring that, by default, only Personal Data necessary for each specific purpose is Processed. This obligation applies to the amount and type of Personal Data collected, the extent of the Processing, the period of storage and accessibility; and
(d) reviewing and updating such measures where necessary to reflect legal, operational and technical developments.
clauses.source_title: Data Protection Law, DIFC Law No. 5 of 2020 (Consolidated Version, July 2025)

clauses.title: Accountability and notification: written data protection policy
clauses.content:
A Controller or Processor that collects or Processes Personal Data shall implement and maintain a data protection policy in writing that is:
(a) proportionate to the extent and type of Processing of Personal Data undertaken; and
(b) consistent with this Law.
clauses.source_title: Data Protection Law, DIFC Law No. 5 of 2020 (Consolidated Version, July 2025)

clauses.title: Records of Processing activities: records of processing
clauses.source_title: Data Protection Law, DIFC Law No. 5 of 2020 (Consolidated Version, July 2025)

clauses.title: Joint Controllers: joint controller agreement
clauses.content: Joint Controllers shall, by way of legally binding written agreement, define their respective responsibilities for ensuring compliance with the obligations under this Law. Such agreement shall clarify the process for ensuring that a Data Subject can exercise his rights under this Law and for providing a Data Subject with the information referred to in Articles 29 and 30.
clauses.source_title: Data Protection Law, DIFC Law No. 5 of 2020 (Consolidated Version, July 2025)

clauses.title: Processors and Sub-processors: written agreement with a processor
clauses.content: Where Processing is to be carried out on behalf of a Controller by a Processor, the Processing shall be governed by a legally binding written agreement between the Controller and the Processor. A Controller shall only enter into agreements with Processors that provide sufficient assurances to implement appropriate technical and organisational measures that ensure the Processing meets the requirements of this Law and protects a Data Subject’s rights.
clauses.source_title: Data Protection Law, DIFC Law No. 5 of 2020 (Consolidated Version, July 2025)
clauses.guidance: Processing on a controller’s behalf must be governed by a legally binding written agreement, with a processor that gives sufficient assurances of appropriate technical and organisational measures.

clauses.title: Processors and Sub-processors: sub-processors need written authorisation
clauses.content: A Processor may not engage another Processor to act as a Sub-processor without the prior written authorisation of a Controller. A Controller may only give a general written authorisation where it has ensured that conditions are in place to enable appointed Sub-processors (present or future) to provide the assurances under Article 24(1). If a general written authorisation has been given, a Processor shall inform a Controller of any intended changes concerning the addition or replacement of a Sub-processor. A Processor shall take into account any good faith objection raised by a Controller to such intended changes.
clauses.source_title: Data Protection Law, DIFC Law No. 5 of 2020 (Consolidated Version, July 2025)

clauses.title: Processors and Sub-processors: sub-processor agreements
clauses.content: Subject to Article 24(2), a Processor may not engage a Sub-processor for carrying out specific Processing activities on behalf of the Controller, unless a legally binding written agreement containing the requirements set out in Article 24(5) is in place with such Sub-processor that ensures a full delegation of the obligations that the Processor owes to the Controller under the agreement with the Controller in respect of such specific Processing activities.
clauses.source_title: Data Protection Law, DIFC Law No. 5 of 2020 (Consolidated Version, July 2025)

clauses.title: Processors and Sub-processors: liability for sub-processors
clauses.content: Where a Sub-processor fails to fulfil its data protection obligations under an agreement or Applicable Law, the Processor that engaged it shall remain fully liable to a relevant Controller for the performance of the Sub-processor's obligations.
clauses.source_title: Data Protection Law, DIFC Law No. 5 of 2020 (Consolidated Version, July 2025)

clauses.title: Processors and Sub-processors: what the agreement must contain
clauses.source_title: Data Protection Law, DIFC Law No. 5 of 2020 (Consolidated Version, July 2025)
clauses.guidance: The agreement must set out the subject-matter, duration, nature and purpose of processing, the types of personal data and data subjects, and the controller’s rights and obligations; and bind the processor to documented instructions, confidentiality, security, sub-processor conditions, assistance with data subject rights and compliance, deletion or return at the end, information for compliance, and audits.

clauses.title: Processors and Sub-processors: notice of infringing instructions
clauses.content: A Processor or Sub-processor shall immediately inform the Controller or Processor (as applicable) whether, in its opinion, the Processing activity infringes this Law.
clauses.source_title: Data Protection Law, DIFC Law No. 5 of 2020 (Consolidated Version, July 2025)

clauses.title: Processors and Sub-processors: no processing without a written agreement
clauses.content: Both a Controller and Processor are in breach of this Law if they commence mutually agreed Processing activity without a written agreement referred to in Articles 24(1) and 24(3).
clauses.source_title: Data Protection Law, DIFC Law No. 5 of 2020 (Consolidated Version, July 2025)

clauses.title: Confidentiality
clauses.content: A Controller or Processor, and where applicable, a Joint Controller or a Sub-processor, shall take steps to ensure that any person acting under its respective authority that has access to Personal Data shall not Process it except on the instructions of the Controller, unless it is required to do so under Applicable Law.
clauses.source_title: Data Protection Law, DIFC Law No. 5 of 2020 (Consolidated Version, July 2025)

clauses.title: Transfers out of the DIFC: adequate level of protection: transfers with adequate protection
clauses.content:
Processing of Personal Data that involves the transfer of Personal Data from the DIFC to a Third Country or to an International Organisation may take place only if:
(a) an adequate level of protection for that Personal Data is ensured by Applicable Law, as set out in Articles 26(2) and (3), including with respect to onward transfers of Personal Data; or
(b) it takes place in accordance with Article 27.
clauses.source_title: Data Protection Law, DIFC Law No. 5 of 2020 (Consolidated Version, July 2025)

clauses.title: Transfers out of the DIFC in the absence of an adequate level of protection: transfers without adequate protection
clauses.content:
A transfer or a set of transfers of Personal Data to a Third Country or an International Organisation may take place on condition that:
(a) the Controller or Processor in question has provided appropriate safeguards (as described in Article 27(2)), and on condition that enforceable Data Subject rights and effective legal remedies for Data Subjects are available;
(b) one of the specific derogations in Article 27(3) applies; or
(c) the limited circumstances in Article 27(4) apply.
clauses.source_title: Data Protection Law, DIFC Law No. 5 of 2020 (Consolidated Version, July 2025)

clauses.title: Transfers out of the DIFC in the absence of an adequate level of protection: appropriate safeguards
clauses.source_title: Data Protection Law, DIFC Law No. 5 of 2020 (Consolidated Version, July 2025)

clauses.title: Data sharing: sharing in response to requests
clauses.content:
Subject to any other obligations under this Law and, in particular, a Controller’s or Processor’s obligations under Part 2 regarding accountability, transparency and compliance with general data protection principles or Part 4 regarding transfers out of the DIFC, where a Controller or Processor receives a request from any public authority over the person or any part of its Group (“a Requesting Authority”) for the disclosure and transfer of any Personal Data, it should:
(a) exercise reasonable caution and diligence to determine the validity and proportionality of the request, including to ensure that any disclosure of Personal Data in such circumstances is made solely for the purpose of meeting the objectives identified in the request from the Requesting Authority;
(b) assess the impact of the proposed transfer in light of the potential risks to the rights of any affected Data Subject and, where appropriate, implement measures to minimise such risks, including by redacting or minimising the Personal Data transferred to the extent possible or utilising appropriate technical or other measures to safeguard the transfer; and
(c) where reasonably practicable, obtain appropriate written and binding assurances from the Requesting Authority that it will respect the rights of any affected Data Subject and comply with the general data protection principles set out in Part 2 in relation to the Processing of Personal Data by the Requesting Authority.
clauses.source_title: Data Protection Law, DIFC Law No. 5 of 2020 (Consolidated Version, July 2025)

clauses.title: Notification of Personal Data Breaches to the Commissioner: controller notifies the Commissioner
clauses.content: If there is a Personal Data Breach that compromises a Data Subject's confidentiality, security or privacy, the Controller involved shall, as soon as practicable in the circumstances, notify the Personal Data Breach to the Commissioner.
clauses.source_title: Data Protection Law, DIFC Law No. 5 of 2020 (Consolidated Version, July 2025)

clauses.title: Notification of Personal Data Breaches to the Commissioner: processor notifies the controller
clauses.content: A Processor shall notify a relevant Controller without undue delay after becoming aware of a Personal Data Breach.
clauses.source_title: Data Protection Law, DIFC Law No. 5 of 2020 (Consolidated Version, July 2025)

clauses.title: Notification of Personal Data Breaches to a Data Subject: notifying data subjects
clauses.content: When a Personal Data Breach is likely to result in a high risk to the security or rights of a Data Subject, the Controller shall communicate the Personal Data Breach to an affected Data Subject as soon as practicable in the circumstances. If there is an immediate risk of damage to the Data Subject, the Controller shall promptly communicate with the affected Data Subject.
clauses.source_title: Data Protection Law, DIFC Law No. 5 of 2020 (Consolidated Version, July 2025)
